text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, you should get a mostly dry window, though clouds will hang around and a shower could arrive after 8. The official forecast puts the rain chance at 40%, but the models are split sharply, from nearly dry to much wetter, so I’d bring a light rain jacket rather than bet the evening on it. Temperatures slide from the current 70 toward 53 overnight, with the north wind easing some. The lake is a different story, with 15 to 20-knot winds early and waves up to 3 feet, so keep small boats close to shore.

Tomorrow looks like the better outdoor day, mostly sunny and around 72, though a north wind will still run 15 to 20 knots on the broad lake before easing. Sunset plans are fine with a backup layer, but I’d be off the water before dark and save the longer outing for Sunday afternoon.

Mostly sunny but cooler near 68, with a northwest breeze and a crisp, clear night ahead.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Labor Day will be another beautiful day with mostly sunny skies and highs in the mid-70s. Lows will be in the 50s. Tuesday will also be dry and decent. The next chance for rain will be Wednesday. It could be a soaker, but significant weather isn’t expected. This will be followed by the coolest air of the season so far for the end of the week. Thursday will be partly sunny with the chance for showers. Highs will be in the 60s. Isolated frost can’t be ruled out Thursday night into Friday morning for the Adirondacks and Northeast Kingdom, so stay tuned for updates. Friday will be a fall preview with partly sunny skies and highs only in the upper 50s to low 60s. Keep the jackets handy if you’re out during the evenings.
